Only a handful of Burmese officials know of the agreement, and even Prime Minister Nu professes not to have been officially informed. Nu stated flatly in a press conference on 20 December that there was no agreement, and that if there were Chinese Communist troops in Burma who refused to leave, "they would be driven out." Official acknowledgment of this military cooperation would arouse widespread apprehension in Burma.

The 22 May riots in Panama against President de la Guardia's administration have led him to declare a state of siege and may erupt into full-scale revolution. The strong national guard, whose repression of student demonstrations earlier this week resulted in one death and widespread and violent resentment, has announced that it is slowly re-gaining control of Panama City. The guard has orders to kill. The students have been joined in a general strike against the government by labor unions and other groups, but appear to have lost control of the disturbance to hoodlums. The latter are probably incited by powerful opposition politicians [REDACTION 1] who are trying to oust the President. Similar riots are occurring in Colon, the northern terminus of the canal.

The armed forces of El Salvador, under the leadership of the minister of defense, Colonel Castillo Navarette, plan to overthrow the ruling civilian-military junta soon in an attempt to head off a Communist takeover, [REDACTED]. The armed forces, which had been virtually paralyzed by disunity, appear to have been spurred to cooperation by increasingly bold Communist activity in recent weeks. Unrestricted Communist organizational activity among the [REDACTION 1] Salvadoran peasants and the visit to Cuba earlier this month of a group of Salvadoran extremists have particularly heightened the concern of the military.

During the November 1960 neutralization debate, the South Korean government and most informed Koreans publicly opposed neutralization. A majority of South Korean students then seemed inclined to distrust that proposal.

President Thieu asked IBRD to organize an aid consortium for South Vietnam. McNamara agreed that IBRD would take on the task if ADB agreed to join and bank members favored the project. The South Vietnamese government hoped for a conference of prospective donors by July.

Japan had increased its patrols along the Rhee line. South Korea's vice minister of foreign affairs hoped to convince President Rhee to encourage Koreans in Japan to return to South Korea by offering them jobs and homes.

case.query: Representatives of the U.S. and Iranian governments initialed the proposed peaceful nuclear-cooperation agreement on July 11, 1978. Under the proposed accompanying note, when Iran needed to arrange disposition of its spent fuel, if the United States had approved reprocessing another cooperating state's spent fuel for that state's fuel-cycle management after the agreement's entry into force, it would approve reprocessing for comparable Iranian needs in the United Kingdom, France, or another mutually agreed state, with comparable benefits and terms and conditions no less favorable.

case.query: In his October 1 speech, Thieu called first for defense against Communist attack and said that other social problems could only be dealt with fully once the country had survived the Communist threat. In the same speech, President Thieu announced that the press and political-party laws would be amended.
